question: Why did the pilot fail, and what's planned to test it?

failed_criteria.statement: Best WavJEPA layer beats the MFCC baseline
failed_criteria.threshold: gap >= 0.05 balanced accuracy, and paired word-type bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0
failed_criteria.result: best layer 3: 0.5438; MFCC 0.5274; gap +0.0163 (needs >= 0.05); paired word-type bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0154, +0.0561] (lower bound needs > 0)

failed_criteria.statement: Minority-class F1 (/d/) at the best layer
failed_criteria.result: /d/ F1 at layer 3 0.3563 (needs >= 0.45; trivial floors 0.391 always-/d/, 0.327 coin, 0.243 base rate)

findings.statement: 25.1% of joint test sites (2,612) have their lemma in training with the same label; the split is disjoint by word form, not lemma. On the 7,586 lemma-unseen sites the gap to MFCC is +0.030, CI [-0.004, +0.073], still short of criterion 1.
The gap to MFCC's paired word-type bootstrap interval is [-0.015, +0.056]: no evidence of an advantage over MFCC, which is not evidence of none.

findings.cause: Sites aren't what the inventory says
findings.status: ruled out for the sites, not the labels
findings.statement: A blind listening audit of 80 sites heard a flap in 72 of 74 decidable cases (6 /d/ can't-tells), and the right word and a well-placed clip in all 80. The labels come from the dictionary form and can't be heard under a flap, so the audit clears the sites, not the labels.
Retraining the single-axis conditions at joint's training size (about 64% of sites) costs 0.006–0.013 at the best layer, against a 0.108 drop from random to joint.

Sites are 2–4 encoder frames wide (median 3, 27.4 ms). For MFCC, whose 25 ms frames see only local audio (deltas reach ±40 ms), a cue outside those frames, such as the preceding vowel's length, is invisible to the probe. WavJEPA encodes the flap ± 200 ms as one excerpt, so at depth its flap frames can carry that context; for WavJEPA the pilot shows only that the cue wasn't linearly recoverable from those frames. Untested: the phonetic environment axis would test both.
evidenced_by: Environment env-v-flap-v (status: planned) - Both vowels and the flap.

findings.cause: The cue doesn't generalize to unseen words
findings.statement: The drop from random to joint is mostly the word axis: holding out speakers costs little, holding out word types costs most of the gap above chance.

answer:
**Why it failed.** Three criteria missed. The best WavJEPA layer (3, 0.5438) beat MFCC (0.5274) by only +0.016, short of the 0.05 needed, and the bootstrap CI [-0.015, +0.056] crosses zero [crit-rev3-1]. The layer curve was nearly flat, with a 0.025 spread against 0.05 required [crit-rev3-3]. /d/ F1 was 0.356, below 0.45 and below the always-/d/ floor [crit-rev3-4].

The candidate causes carry different statuses:
- **Ruled out:** too little training data, since subsampling cost only 0.006–0.013 [find-training]. The audit also cleared the sites themselves, but not the dictionary-derived labels, which can't be heard under a flap [find-sites].
- **Consistent with the result:** the cue doesn't generalize to unseen words. Holding out word types accounts for most of the drop [find-words].
- **Limitations:** lemma overlap affects 25.1% of test sites, yet lemma-unseen sites still fall short at +0.030 [find-lemma]. Low power also applies: the result is no evidence of an advantage, which is not evidence of none [find-power].
- **Open:** sites are only 2–4 frames wide, so context cues such as preceding-vowel length may be invisible to MFCC, or not linearly recoverable from WavJEPA's flap frames [find-width].

**What's planned.** The only planned test in the rows is the phonetic-environment axis (env-v-flap-v, covering both vowels and the flap). It is meant to test the site-width explanation for both models [find-width]. The rows show no planned tests for the other causes.
